method: An event-year is a calendar year in which (a) the currency's December-average dollar rate implies a loss of 30% or more of its dollar value on the previous December (BIS monthly averages, WS_XRU; for the US the BIS broad nominal effective index), (b) December year-on-year CPI inflation reaches 33.3%, i.e. a 25% loss of purchasing power (BIS WS_LONG_CPI; World Bank annual averages where BIS has no series), or (c) a national deposit freeze, bank holiday or withdrawal limit of three days or more begins (Laeven and Valencia, IMF WP/18/206; India's 2016 demonetisation added). For the forecast I count currency-or-freeze years in 1995-2025, weighting year y by 0.5^((2025-y)/15), which gives 16.86 weighted years; transition-era and pre-euro national-currency events fall before 1995 or are excluded. Each country's rate is the gamma-Poisson posterior (0.5 + weighted events)/(0.5/g + 16.86), where g is the pooled weighted rate of the 46 countries' own records in the country's current S&P band: 0.2% for AAA/AA+ issuers plus sterling and the yen (0 events in 310 country-years; equal to the us preset), 1.0% for AA to A- (Korea 1997 and 2008, Iceland 2008), 1.75% for BBB (Indonesia 1997-98, Mexico 1995, India 2016), 6.5% for BB (Brazil, South Africa, Turkey), 25% for B (Argentina, Nigeria); for euro members 0.14%, 0.35% and 0.7% for AAA/AA+, AA to A- and BBB, which average to the pooled euro-area freeze rate (Greece 2015, Cyprus 2013: about 0.35% a year). Present conditions enter through the current rating and, for three countries only, through a stated multiplier (Argentina 0.84 from the central bank survey's exchange-rate forecast, Turkey 0.6 from its CDS and managed lira, Nigeria 0.7 from the floated naira) and, where inflation is close to 33.3% now (Argentina 33.1%, Turkey 29.8% in October 2026), an added chance that inflation alone crosses the threshold. The pessimistic figure is the forecast's odds times 10^(0.39 - 0.25(log10 odds + 0.75)), a curve fitted to the three preset pairs. The 5th and 95th percentiles are interpolated in log p from the presets' own ranges.

reproduced.basis: No US event-year since 1933: the broad dollar's worst 12-month fall since 1994 is 10.4% (https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_EER/1.0/M.N.B.US), inflation peaked at 13.5% in 1980, no freeze since the 1933 holiday. Prior 0.2% (zero events in 310 country-years of the ten AAA/AA+ or reserve-currency issuers); 0.5/(0.5/0.002 + 16.86) = 0.19%.

anchors.comment: Preset 0.002 (0.0003-0.01): reproduced. The 0.2% prior for this band was set equal to the preset, so this is a consistency check rather than an independent test; the pooled zero in 310 country-years allows anything up to about 1% at 95%.

reproduced.basis: The pessimist curve fitted to the three preset pairs gives odds x 7.4 at 0.19%.

anchors.comment: Preset 0.015 (0.004-0.04): reproduced by construction, since the curve is fitted to the presets. The preset's own reasoning (a 10% a year US debt crisis, of which 15% reach this threshold) is the scenario behind it.

reproduced.basis: Population-weighted mean of my figures for Germany, France, the UK, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, Belgium, Portugal, Greece, Sweden, Austria, Switzerland, Denmark, Finland, Norway and Ireland (about 430 million people; populations approximate): 0.29%.

anchors.comment: Preset 0.003 (0.0005-0.012): reproduced. The euro priors are set from the pooled euro-area freeze rate, not from the preset; Italy (0.57%) and Greece (1.3%) carry a third of the weighted total.

reproduced.basis: Population-weighted mean of the same 16 countries' pessimistic figures: 1.9%.

Argentina by the same method: currency-or-freeze part 0.32 from 1995-2025, cut to 0.27 for present conditions; plus a 0.2 chance that inflation alone exceeds 33.3% in the next 12 months: 0.27 + 0.73 x 0.2 = 0.42.

anchors.comment: Preset 0.15 (0.07-0.3): my figure is 1.8 times higher on the currency-or-freeze part alone and 2.8 times higher in all. Three reasons. BIS December averages put 2016 at 30.1% and 2024 at 37.1%, and the December 2001 freeze is an event-year of its own, so there are 8 events in 1995-2025, not 5. My weights favour recent years, which were Argentina's worst. And the preset reads inflation as 23.6% in the year to September; that is the January-September cumulative. INDEC's year-on-year rate was 33.4% in September and 33.1% in October 2026 (https://www.forbesargentina.com/money/subio-inflacion-octubre-ubico-22-n102387), right at the 33.3% that a 25% loss of purchasing power means. Checker: two of the three reasons need correcting. First, the 2024 event is the devaluation of 13 December 2023 counted a second time: the December 2023 average mixes 12 days at about 365 pesos with 19 at about 805. End-of-December rates (808.48 on 29 December 2023, 1,032.5 on 30 December 2024, BIS daily WS_XRU D.AR.ARS.A) give a 21.7% loss in 2024. Without it the history gives 0.27, not 0.32; the final currency-or-freeze 0.27 comes from the central bank survey and does not change. Third, the 23.6% is indeed the January-September cumulative (iProfesional, 3 November 2026: 'la inflacion alcanzo el 23,6% hasta septiembre'), but it appears only in a source claim of the step-3 file: the preset's 0.15 uses no inflation figure, and its definition excludes 'inflation that deposit interest roughly matches'. On the preset's own definition the comparison is 0.27 against 0.15; the extra 0.15 from the inflation-only branch is a difference of definition, not a misreading.

Preset 0.3 (0.15-0.5). Higher for the same reasons as the forecast; 0.55 is also the share of 2016-2025 years with an event (6 currency years and 2 inflation-only years out of 10, less a discount for the present band regime). Checker: 2024 is an inflation-only year (December inflation 118%) rather than a currency year (see the forecast comment), so the count is 5 and 3, still 8 of 10.

countries.name: Australia

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: No event-year in 1995-2025: the Australian dollar's worst December-on-December fall was 23% (2008), inflation stayed low, no freeze (https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_XRU/1.0/M.AU..A; https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/wp/2018/wp18206.pdf). AAA prior 0.2%: 0.5/(0.5/0.002 + 16.86) = 0.19%.

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve fitted to the presets: odds x 7.4. Scenario: a China-led commodity and housing bust that takes the currency down 30% in a year, which 2008 approached.

countries.notes: S&P AAA. The 2008 fall (23%) is the closest call; a commodity-currency shock is the main path.

countries.name: Austria

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: Euro member since 1999; no freeze or holiday (https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/wp/2018/wp18206.pdf) and the euro's worst December-on-December fall against the dollar is under 20% (https://stats.bis.org). Euro AAA/AA+ prior 0.14%: 0.5/(0.5/0.0014 + 16.86) = 0.13%.

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve fitted to the presets: odds x 8.5. Scenario: a euro break-up or a Cyprus-style bail-in reaching a core member.

countries.notes: S&P AA+. Banking crisis 2008 (Laeven-Valencia) without any loss of deposit access.

countries.name: Belgium

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: Euro member since 1999; no freeze or holiday (https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/wp/2018/wp18206.pdf); the euro never fell 30% in a year (https://stats.bis.org). Euro AA-to-A- prior 0.35%: 0.5/(0.5/0.0035 + 16.86) = 0.31%.

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve: odds x 6.8. Rogoff names Belgium, with the UK and France, as a candidate for a debt crisis (https://247wallst.com/personal-finance/2026/08/29/a-harvard-economist-says-the-debt-reckoning-is-coming-and-names-who-pays-for-it/, via the step-3 file).

countries.notes: S&P AA-. Fortis and Dexia were rescued in 2008 without any freeze.

countries.name: Canada

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: No event-year since 1970: the Canadian dollar never fell 20% December-on-December, inflation stayed low, no systemic banking crisis in Laeven-Valencia (https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_XRU/1.0/M.CA..A; https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/wp/2018/wp18206.pdf). AAA prior: 0.19%.

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve: odds x 7.4.

countries.notes: S&P AAA. Tied to the US dollar; a US crisis is the main path.

countries.name: Chile

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: Events in 1982, 1984 and 1985 (peso down 46%, 31% and 31%; https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_XRU/1.0/M.CL..A) but none since 1995 (worst 23%, 2008). Band prior for S&P A 1.0%: 0.5/(0.5/0.01 + 16.86) = 0.75%; spread 87 points in August 2026, the lowest in Latin America after Uruguay (https://www.bloomberglinea.com/mercados/asi-cerro-el-riesgo-pais-en-america-latina-en-agosto-argentina-y-uruguay-en-los-extremos/).

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve: odds x 5.4. Scenario: a copper collapse with a 2008-sized peso fall that goes further.

countries.notes: S&P A. Free float and inflation targeting since 1999; the 1980s debt crisis is outside the window.

countries.name: Colombia

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: One event since 1970 (1985, peso down 33%) and none since 1995; the 2015 fall was 28% (https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_XRU/1.0/M.CO..A). BB band prior 6.5%: 0.5/(0.5/0.065 + 16.86) = 2.0%.

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve: odds x 4.2. Scenario: the fiscal slippage behind S&P's April 2026 downgrade to BB- turns into a run on the peso, as the 28% fall of 2015 nearly did.

countries.notes: S&P cut Colombia to BB- in April 2026 (search snippet of the S&P release); spread 189 points in August 2026; the peso rose 21% against the dollar in the year to October 2026 (BIS), so present pressure is low.

countries.name: Costa Rica

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve: odds x 4.2.

countries.notes: S&P BB, Fitch positive outlook; spread 127 points in August 2026; the colon rose 12% in the year to September 2026. Many deposits are in dollars, which shields them from a colon fall but not from a freeze.

countries.name: Germany

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: No event since 1970 (https://stats.bis.org; https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/wp/2018/wp18206.pdf). Euro AAA prior 0.14%: 0.13%.

countries.name: Greece

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: One event since 1995: the 2015 bank holiday of 21 days and withdrawal limits (https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/wp/2018/wp18206.pdf), weight 0.63. Euro BBB prior 0.7%: (0.5 + 0.63)/(0.5/0.007 + 16.86) = 1.3%.

countries.name: Hungary

countries.name: Iceland

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: Events in 1980, 1982, 1983 and 2008 (krona down 50% December-on-December in 2008; https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_XRU/1.0/M.IS..A); weight 0.46 since 1995. A+ band prior 1.0%: (0.5 + 0.46)/(50 + 16.86) = 1.4%.

countries.name: Japan

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve: odds x 7.4. Scenario: a bond-market revolt against debt of about 230% of GDP that the Bank of Japan meets by printing, taking the yen down 30% in a year.

countries.name: Turkey

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: Currency events 1995-99, 2001, 2021 and 2023 (lira down 34-53%; https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_XRU/1.0/M.TR..A), weight 3.45: posterior with the BB prior 16%, times 0.6 for the managed lira (15% loss in the year to October 2026) and CDS of 217 points (https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/turkiyes-cds-falls-to-lowest-level-in-6-5-months-226086) = 9.6%. Inflation was 29.77% in October 2026 with 2.58% that month (https://www.anews.com.tr/turkey/2026/11/03/turkiyes-annual-consumer-inflation-stands-at-2977-in-october/amp); a 0.25 chance it alone passes 33.3% gives 0.096 + 0.904 x 0.25 = 0.32.

countries.notes: S&P BB-. Inflation-only years (2000, 2022, 2024) are not in the history count; they enter through today's inflation instead. About 0.23 of the 0.32 is the inflation-only branch, in which lira deposits paying near-inflation rates lose little: see openQuestions. Checker: the CDS figure (217 points) is from 26 August 2026, not current; the article says it was the lowest since 18 February.

countries.notes: S&P AA. Placed with the AAA band as a reserve-currency issuer. Northern Rock (2007) queues lasted days but deposits stayed usable.

countries.name: United States

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: No event-year since the 1933 bank holiday; the broad dollar's worst 12-month fall since 1994 is 10.4% (https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_EER/1.0/M.N.B.US). AA+ prior 0.2%: 0.19%; inflation 3.7% in September 2026 (BIS WS_LONG_CPI).

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve: odds x 7.4, the same as the preset's Dalio-Rogoff scenario (10% a year debt crisis x 15% crossing the threshold).

countries.notes: S&P AA+. Matches the preset.

countries.name: Argentina

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: Currency-or-freeze years 2001, 2002, 2016, 2018, 2019, 2022, 2023, 2024 (https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_XRU/1.0/M.AR..A; freezes 1989 and 2001 in https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/wp/2018/wp18206.pdf) give 32%; the October 2026 central bank survey expects 1,985 pesos per dollar in October 2027 against 2,216 for a 30% loss from 1,551 (https://perfil.com/economia/rem-del-bcra-el-precio-que-le-ponen-a-la-inflacion-y-al-dolar-45-actores-del-mercado-a9fcc7k2dRuP), about 0.27 at 15-20% volatility. Inflation is 33.1% a year (https://www.forbesargentina.com/money/subio-inflacion-octubre-ubico-22-n102387); a 0.2 chance it alone passes 33.3% gives 0.27 + 0.73 x 0.2 = 0.42. Checker: 2024 is the 13 December 2023 devaluation counted twice by December averaging (end-of-December rates give a 21.7% loss in 2024, BIS daily); without it the history gives 0.27 and the survey multiplier becomes about 1.0, so the currency-or-freeze 0.27 stands. The same survey expects 21.8% inflation over the next 12 months (top ten forecasters 23.2%) and 30.4% for 2026; the 0.2 chance that inflation alone passes 33.3% should be read against that. Figure not changed: see openQuestions on whether the inflation-only branch belongs here at all.

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve applied to 0.42; 8 of the 10 years 2016-2025 met the threshold by currency or inflation (BIS).

countries.notes: S&P B-. Three times the buenosAires preset (0.15); see the anchor comments. The survey has under-forecast monthly inflation (1.8% expected for October, 2.2% printed). About 0.15 of the 0.42 is the inflation-only branch.

countries.name: Brazil

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: Currency events 1999, 2002 and 2015 (real down 35%, 35% and 32% December-on-December; https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_XRU/1.0/M.BR..A), weight 1.28; the 1990 freeze and 1980-94 hyperinflation fall before the window. BB prior 6.5%: (0.5 + 1.28)/(7.7 + 16.86) = 7.2%.

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve: odds x 3.0. Scenario: fiscal dominance after the 2026 election, a 2002 or 2015 rerun.

countries.notes: S&P BB; spread 174 points in August 2026; the real rose 5% in the year to October 2026. The real is a high-beta currency: three falls just over 30% in 17 years, each partly reversed.

countries.name: China

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: No event since 1995; the 1994 unification (official rate down 31.5%) is excluded, as in Laeven-Valencia, because most trade already used the swap rate (https://www.imf.org/-/media/files/publications/wp/2018/wp18206.pdf; https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_XRU/1.0/M.CN..A). A+ prior 1.0% (the yuan is not freely convertible, so not in the reserve band): 0.75%.

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve: odds x 5.4. Scenario: a property-and-local-debt crisis met by a step devaluation, or sanctions in a Taiwan crisis freezing foreign-currency access.

countries.notes: S&P A+. The 2022 Henan rural-bank freeze locked hundreds of thousands of depositors' accounts for months (recalled); regional freezes of this kind add risk for a small share of households that a national count does not capture.

countries.name: India

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: One event since 1995: demonetisation, with withdrawals capped at Rs 24,000 a week from 14 November 2016 until 13 March 2017 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Indian_banknote_demonetisation), weight 0.66; the rupee never fell 30% December-on-December (https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_XRU/1.0/M.IN..A). BBB prior 1.75%: (0.5 + 0.66)/(28.6 + 16.86) = 2.6%.

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve: odds x 3.9.

countries.notes: S&P BBB. Without counting demonetisation the figure would be 1.1%. The rupee was at a record 95.5 per dollar in October 2026, 7% down on the year (BIS): pressure, but far from 30%.

countries.name: Indonesia

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: Events 1997 (rupiah down 51%) and 1998 (37%, inflation 78%) December-on-December (https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_XRU/1.0/M.ID..A), weight 0.56. BBB prior 1.75%: (0.5 + 0.56)/(28.6 + 16.86) = 2.3%.

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve: odds x 4.1. Scenario: fiscal-rule and central-bank-independence worries turn the 2025-26 slide into a run.

countries.notes: S&P BBB. The rupiah was near a record 18,000 per dollar in October 2026, 8% down on the year (BIS).

countries.name: Nigeria

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: Currency events 1999, 2016, 2023 and 2024 (naira down 78%, 36%, 50% and 42%; https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_XRU/1.0/M.NG..A), weight 2.83: posterior with the B prior 17.6%, times 0.7 because the naira now floats and rose 13% in the year to August 2026 while inflation fell to 14.06% (https://gazettengr.com/nigerias-inflation-rate-dropped-to-14-06-in-october-nbs/) = 12%.

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve applied to 0.12: an oil-price collapse with a return to rationed dollars.

countries.notes: S&P B- (Fitch and Moody's B/B3 in 2025). In early 2023 cash withdrawals were capped and new notes scarce for weeks; that year is already a currency event. The 0.7 multiplier is a judgment. Checker: 17.6% is the posterior, not the prior (the B prior is 25%). The 1999 event is the abolition of the official rate in favour of the market rate, a unification like China's 1994 one, which this file excludes; Laeven and Valencia date Nigeria's currency crises 1983, 1989, 1997 and 2016, not 1999. Treating 1999 as China's 1994 is treated (and dropping Argentina's double-counted 2024 from the B prior) gives 0.11 instead of 0.12; not changed, as the difference is inside the range.

countries.name: Philippines

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: Events 1983-84 but none since 1995; the 1997 fall was 29%, just under the threshold (https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_XRU/1.0/M.PH..A). BBB+ band prior 1.75%: 0.5/(28.6 + 16.86) = 1.1%.

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve: odds x 4.9.

countries.notes: S&P BBB+. An energy importer hit by the 2026 oil shock; the peso was 8% down on the year to October 2026.

countries.name: South Africa

bankingCrisis.forecast.basis: Currency events 2001 (rand down 34%) and 2008 (32%) December-on-December (https://stats.bis.org/api/v2/data/dataflow/BIS/WS_XRU/1.0/M.ZA..A), weight 0.79; 2015 was 23%. BB prior 6.5%: (0.5 + 0.79)/(7.7 + 16.86) = 5.2%.

bankingCrisis.pessimistic.basis: Pessimist curve: odds x 3.2.

countries.notes: S&P BB (positive). Deep, liquid rand market: it falls hard in global shocks and recovers.

blockedSources: https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/PCPIEPCH (Access Denied, and 'Blob not found' on other routes): WEO end-of-period inflation and 2026-27 projections for every country; I used BIS monthly CPI and World Bank annual averages instead, and no projections except Argentina's survey.
https://www.worldgovernmentbonds.com/sovereign-cds/ (table loads by script): five-year CDS for all countries; I have spreads only for Latin America (Bloomberg Linea, end of August 2026) and Turkey.

Laeven-Valencia dataset spreadsheet (per-episode deposit-freeze and holiday dates): not opened. The paper's text gives 8 freezes (most recent Cyprus 2013, Ukraine 2014, Greece 2015) and 6 holidays; Argentina's dates come from the step-3 file; Brazil's 1990 freeze is recalled and changes no count, since 1990 is a currency year anyway.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_credit_rating: S&P column read; Fitch partly and Moody's not; the page says the tables are not fully updated. Colombia's April 2026 downgrade to BB- and Hungary's May 2026 affirmation are search snippets.
openQuestions: The purchasing-power criterion (a 25% loss, i.e. 33.3% inflation in a year) puts Argentina (33.1% now) and Turkey (29.8%) at the threshold, so a third or more of their figures is the chance that steady inflation crosses a line, with no crisis. Deposits there earn close to inflation, so the loss share the model attaches to bankingCrisis (35% in Buenos Aires) is far too high for that branch. Either drop the criterion for chronic inflation, or give inflation-only events their own small loss share. Currency-or-freeze only: Argentina 0.27, Turkey 0.10.

The buenosAires preset (0.15) rests on reading 23.6% as year-on-year inflation; it is the January-September 2026 cumulative. By its own definition the preset should be about 0.4 (0.27 currency-or-freeze only). Checker: not so. The preset's definition (research/step3/tail-finance-unrest.json, buenosAires) says 'Exchange controls alone, and inflation that deposit interest roughly matches, do not count', and its basis uses no inflation figure; the mislabelled 23.6% appears only in a source claim of that file. On the preset's own definition the comparable figure is the currency-or-freeze 0.27 (pessimistic 0.43 by the same curve), and Turkey's is 0.10 (pessimistic 0.23). Which definition governs is for the model's owner: the brief's wording includes the purchasing-power test without that exclusion.

presetFor sends every unlisted middle-income country to buenosAires, and so to 0.15 a year. By this method listed middle-income countries without Argentina's history get 0.7-2.6% (Chile, China, Mexico, Colombia, Costa Rica, Philippines, India, Indonesia). Unlisted countries (Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam, Peru, Morocco...) should get a separate default, for example the BBB/BB prior of 1-2%, not Argentina's figure; frontier economies with recent crises (Egypt, Pakistan, Ghana, Sri Lanka, Lebanon) would need their own.

December-average changes miss falls that peak inside the year and partly reverse. Over any rolling 12 months of monthly averages (BIS) Colombia lost 37% to August 2015 (28% December-on-December), Poland 36% to March 2009, the Philippines 38% to January 1998; Turkey's August 2018 fall is also missed. Counting those would roughly double the figures for Colombia, Poland and the Philippines. I kept December averages because the preset used them.
Withdrawal limits without a bank holiday: India 2016 and Nigeria 2023 are counted. Without India's the Indian figure would be 1.1% instead of 2.6%.

Euro members share one currency, so a break-up would hit all of them in the same year; the figures are per household and need no correlation, but a reader comparing countries should know the euro priors are one pooled rate split by rating.
